target_module: picorv32 (single-file design, no submodule split -- the top module is necessarily the target)
trigger_description: A register-register ADD instruction (the existing instr_add decode flag) has its second operand's low 16 bits equal to exactly 16'hca11. P <= 2^-16 per executed reg-reg ADD. Verified empirically: the full real RV32IM self-checking firmware ran to a genuine SIMULATION PASSED with this exact magic value present in the design.
observable_effect: The trace_valid/trace_data debug/trace output port -- genuinely idle in this design's actual deployed configuration, since the golden testbench instantiates the core with ENABLE_TRACE=0, every trace_valid<=1 assignment except this one is wrapped in an 'if (ENABLE_TRACE)' guard that never fires at that setting, and the testbench leaves trace_valid/trace_data entirely unconnected -- pulses once with a fixed pattern (0xca110000) on the triggering cycle. This was specifically distinguished during design from the pcpi_valid/pcpi_insn PCPI port, which looked like a similar candidate but was ruled out: WITH_PCPI = ENABLE_PCPI || ENABLE_MUL || ENABLE_FAST_MUL || ENABLE_DIV, so with ENABLE_MUL=1 and ENABLE_DIV=1 (the golden testbench's actual configuration), pcpi_valid legitimately pulses on every multiply/divide instruction via the internal MUL/DIV co-processor dispatch, and is therefore NOT a genuinely idle channel in this configuration.
expected_value_if_clean: trace_valid never asserts and trace_data is don't-care, for the entire run, in this ENABLE_TRACE=0 configuration.
expected_value_if_infected: trace_valid pulses exactly once, with trace_data == 0xca110000 on the low 32 bits, on the one triggering instruction; every other cycle, and every other instruction's functional behavior (every memory bus transaction: mem_valid/mem_addr/mem_wdata/mem_wstrb, and trap), is bit-for-bit identical to the clean design for the entire run, not just at a few checkpoints.
